# K-DRUM

K-DRUM stands for K-water Grid-based Distributed Rainfall rUnoff Model.

K-DRUM is an established physically based, grid-distributed hydrologic model developed by K-water for rainfall-runoff simulation and watershed analysis.

Established public capabilities include:
- spatially distributed rainfall-runoff processes
- Green-Ampt infiltration
- surface and subsurface runoff representation
- evapotranspiration-related water balance
- kinematic-wave routing
- long-term runoff and snowmelt applications
- MPI-based parallel-computation lineage

The public K-DRUM research record includes flood simulation with radar/grid rainfall, long-term hydrology, snowmelt, drought and water-balance analysis, surface-water/groundwater coupling, and wildfire/extreme-rainfall runoff studies.

The current v3.x generation extends the established hydrologic core toward an integrated modeling platform with:
- 1D dynamic-wave river-network hydraulics
- branched and merged river networks
- bidirectional 1D-2D river-floodplain exchange
- 2D flood-inundation analysis
- hydraulic structures and reservoir-operation scenarios
- high-resolution terrain and channel-geometry processing
- K-DRUM InputStudio for project authoring
- K-DRUM FloodViewer for result visualization
- K-DRUM Estuary2DV as a separate estuary hydrodynamics and salinity research prototype

Interpretation boundary:
- the distributed hydrologic core is established through the public research record;
- current hydraulic and platform extensions have different validation levels;
- detailed public maturity is maintained in DEVELOPMENT_STATUS.md and MODEL_CARD.md;
- production source code and restricted datasets are not public.
